title: corpus/held-out/<plan>.json
description: The held-out partition's own interaction plan steps and oracles (Story 1.51, AD-9, AD-22), which evaluation.json's partitionPlan.heldOutPlan names. The held-out and both views append interactionPlan and oracles (and the optional rubrics, waivers and mappings) to contract.json's and add behaviorOracles to each named behavior; a development run never opens this file. Each step and oracle has the shape eval-quality's contract gives it, and the engine's compile over the held-out view is what judges them; tea-evaluate check validates each against the contract schema in the view and names a path or an ID, never a value. The tea-evaluate runtime owns this schema.

interactionPlan.description: Steps only the held-out partition runs, appended after the shared steps. A step's stepId must differ from every stepId of contract.json, and its after clause may name a shared or a held-out step only.

oracles.description: Oracles over the held-out steps (or shared ones). Each leaves no trace in the development partition. An oracle's ID must differ from every oracle ID of contract.json.

rubrics.description: Rubrics whose criteria only the held-out partition judges (Story 1.105), appended to contract.json's rubrics in the held-out and both views. Each has the shape eval-quality's contract gives a rubric, and a criterion's evidence pointer must name a step the held-out view declares: a shared step or a held-out one. A rubric's ID must differ from every rubric ID of contract.json. A criterion in contract.json belongs to the development partition, and to the held-out one too unless it reads a development-only step. Omit the field when the held-out partition judges nothing of its own.

waivers.description: Waivers only the held-out partition carries (Story 1.106), appended to contract.json's waivers in the held-out and both views. Each has the shape eval-quality's contract gives a waiver. A waiver names a discipline rule and no oracle, so its condition is the only field that reads a step: when the condition names a step by an interaction pointer, that step must be one the held-out view declares, a shared step or a held-out one. A waiver's ID must differ from every waiver ID of contract.json. A waiver in contract.json belongs to the development partition, and to the held-out one too unless its condition reads a development-only step. Omit the field when the held-out partition waives nothing of its own.

mappings.description: Evaluator mapping rows only the held-out partition reads (Story 1.107), added to evaluator/mapping.json's rows in the held-out and both views, for a command or sealed-brief-agent evaluator. A row has the key the evaluator prints and the binding evaluator/mapping.json gives a key: an oracle and the behavior it answers, or a rubric criterion and its anchored scale levels. A row's key must differ from every key of evaluator/mapping.json and from the other rows', and it binds an oracle or criterion the held-out view declares and no other key binds: a row for an oracle or criterion of the held-out plan belongs here, since evaluator/mapping.json is read by the development partition, which must hold no held-out ID. A row of evaluator/mapping.json that binds an oracle or criterion of contract.json belongs to the development partition, and to the held-out one too unless the held-out view drops what it binds. Omit the field when the held-out partition binds nothing of its own.

behaviorOracles.description: The oracle IDs each behavior gains in the held-out view, keyed by behaviorId. Every behavior keeps at least one oracle there, because the engine compiles each behavior against the oracles it names; a behavior whose only oracle reads a development-only step needs an entry here.
